item.title: Participation in the European EuroHPC DARE Project
item.description:
Participation in the European DARE project (HPC Digital Autonomy with RISC-V in Europe), selected under the EuroHPC JU (Joint Undertaking).

This project aims to strengthen Europe’s strategic and technological autonomy in high-performance computing (HPC) by designing and optimizing software stacks and numerical algorithms tailored to European processors based on the open RISC-V instruction set architecture.

Within this project, our work focuses in particular on:

  • Developing and optimizing parallel sparse linear algebra libraries and algorithms.
  • Adapting computational kernels and direct/hybrid factorization methods to accelerated and vector RISC-V architectures.
  • Evaluating performance at exascale in collaboration with European academic and industrial partners.

item.title: PhD Defense: Clément Richefort
item.description:
Clément Richefort successfully defended his PhD thesis in Computer Science on November 28, 2024, at Bordeaux University (LaBRI).

  • Title: Development of an algebraic multigrid solver for the indefinite Helmholtz equation
  • Supervision: Pierre Ramet (PhD advisor, 100% supervision)
  • Funding: CEA grant
  • Institution: Bordeaux University / LaBRI

His research focused on designing and evaluating algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods tailored to the indefinite Helmholtz equation, as well as leveraging mixed-precision arithmetic to accelerate the solution of large sparse linear systems arising from numerical simulations.

Clément Richefort is currently a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC, Germany).

item.title: HybQuant Initiative: Quantum Hub in Nouvelle-Aquitaine
item.description:
The Nouvelle-Aquitaine Quantum Hub (HybQuant) project has been selected under the national HQI (France Hybrid HPC Quantum Initiative) call.

Pierre Ramet contributed to setting up this major regional initiative and is actively involved in the scientific and technological organization of the project.

HybQuant aims to:

  • Bring together regional academic and industrial stakeholders around the hybridization of classical high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing.
  • Develop software and algorithmic bridges enabling joint use of supercomputers and quantum processors/emulators (QPUs).
  • Train and support the scientific community in new programming paradigms and hybrid quantum-classical linear algebra.

item.title: Build PaStiX with Guix-HPC
item.description:
How to build PaStiX

The package definitions in the Guix-HPC repository extend . To make them available to guix command-line tools, create the ~/.config/guix/channels.scm file with the following snippet to configure the guix-hpc channel:

(cons (channel
        (name 'guix-hpc)
        (url "https://gitlab.inria.fr/guix-hpc/guix-hpc.git"))
      %default-channels)

That way, guix pull will systematically update not only Guix, but also Guix-HPC.

guix package -u pastix

Hacking on Guix-HPC

When working on packages of the guix-hpc channel, you’ll need to clone the guix-hpc repository:

cd src
git clone https://gitlab.inria.fr/guix-hpc/guix-hpc.git

From then on, you can edit package definitions, and then try them out by passing the location of the checkout using the -L flag to guix build and other command-line tools, as in this example:

guix build -L ~/src/guix-hpc pastix
